history.summary: A well-built CapitaLand 1,044 sqft 2BR at $1,724 psf, essentially at the $1,705 median (no PSF discount), 430m from Serangoon MRT (NEL/CCL interchange). Strong 7.4%/yr resale CAGR on 82 txns and a quality, well-maintained estate, but $1.8M at full median PSF leaves little entry cushion, and the score_1000 of 611 is the weakest in the batch. A fair-priced quality asset rather than a value buy.
history.rating_rationale: Genuinely good fundamentals — CapitaLand build quality (marble/granite finishes, well-kept after 20+ years), 430m to the Serangoon NEL/Circle Line interchange (NEX mall), and 7.4%/yr resale CAGR. But the listing is priced AT the URA median ($1,724 vs $1,705), so there is no value gap to capture, and at $1.8M the entry is high for a 2003 leasehold 2BR. The technical score (611, lowest in batch) flags that the price already reflects the quality. Solid hold but not asymmetric — the upside is paid for. Neutral.

history.summary: CapitaLand-built, well-maintained 2003 condo a genuine 5-min/430m walk to Serangoon MRT and NEX mall, priced exactly at the URA median (PSF 1705 vs 1705) at a $2M quantum. Solid location and 7.4%/yr resale CAGR, but at-median pricing, a 23-year age, and only an off-frontier technical read make it a fairly-priced Neutral rather than a value Buy.
history.rating_rationale: Location is the strength: 430m to Serangoon MRT (NEL interchange) and NEX, with reliable CapitaLand build and good upkeep reviews. 7.4%/yr resale CAGR on 82 txns is healthy. But there is no value edge here — PSF 1705 is dead-on the URA median, so you pay full freight, and at 23 years old (2003) the building is mid-life with worn exterior noted in reviews. $2M quantum is fine for liquidity but the unit is off the efficiency frontier (off_frontier, MMR 1520). Good home-quality asset, but as an investment it's priced to market with no discount and limited room to outrun the district.
